event_model_payload.headline: Wo Long 2: Wings Of Ember Made Me Rethink My Relationship With Soulslikes
event_model_payload.summary:
I went into my hands-on session with Wo Long 2: Wings of Ember expecting to hate it. That probably isn't the sort of sentence Team Ninja wants associated with its upcoming action-RPG, but it's an important one. I've never been great at souls-likes. The combination of punishing enemies, precise timing, complicated combat systems, and the possibility that something resembling an eldritch horror might annihilate me in three hits is not my idea of a fun time. Wo Long 2 initially looked like it was going to be another game determined to make me suffer. Instead, I had a surprisingly great time and walked away from my Gamescom preview eager to play more.

The sequel to 2023's Wo Long: Fallen Dynasty is still built around fast, demanding martial-arts combat, with deflection remaining a crucial part of surviving encounters. After my demo, I went back and played the original, and found it to be far more approachable than I remembered. However, Team Ninja has made some significant changes since Fallen Dynasty that mean I can already confidently say that Wings of Ember feels like a far superior game to its predecessor.

My problem with souls-likes isn't necessarily that they're difficult; it's that they refuse to explain themselves. That's great for gamers who enjoy throwing themselves at things repeatedly until they figure them out, but that's not me. Wo Long 2 is more than happy to teach you its ways without holding your hand and making things trivial.

My hands-on session gave me plenty of information about its combat systems, and the tutorials are considerably more useful than simply throwing a paragraph of text at you before sending you off to your untimely death. There's a lot to take in, but the game gradually explains how its different mechanics interact rather than expecting you to instinctively understand the entire combat system, and that made a huge difference when it came to my enjoyment.

The most notable change is that rather than following the linear design of the original, Wo Long 2 features a vast open world with plenty to discover and no "right" order to discover it all in. That change is exactly what made it click for me. Instead of progressing through one level of enemies after another, Wo Long 2 gives you far more freedom to explore its battlefields. Instead of approaching the game focusing on just surviving, I found myself wondering, "What's over there?" and going off on short exploration quests of my own making. It's that approach that made Elden Ring click for so many people, and in a similar vein, Nioh 3 from the same developer.

That was really rewarding at times, too. By completely ignoring the main objective marker and heading to a nearby area that piqued my interest, I stumbled across a tiny squirrel demon in an oversized dragon outfit, called a Fengli. It had a vaguely ridiculous expression, and when I approached it, it started a minigame where I had to parry it to get it to freeze and drop a bunch of rewards. And you can pet it! The loot made stopping to investigate every corner of the map feel worthwhile, and the squirrel was the cutest thing I've ever encountered in a souls-like--that alone probably pushes Wo Long 2 into my official considerations for Game of the Year, because I'm a sucker for cute creatures.

It reminded me of the first game's Shitieshou--a panda-like demon that's completely harmless and grants you a reward by feeding it equipment. They're present in Wo Long 2 too, much to my delight.

The world is still packed with enemies, flags, outposts, and encounters, but exploration isn't just about wandering around and finding pretty things. The Morale system is back, and capturing outposts and raising Battle Flags can strengthen you and give you more reason to explore before taking on tougher enemies further on. It also gives me options when I'm struggling--if I run into something that flattens me immediately, I don't have to keep throwing myself at it. I can go elsewhere, explore, and make myself stronger. Or find another squirrel.

Of course, the game hasn't suddenly transformed into a cozy open-world adventure about befriending cute creatures. Wo Long 2 still needs you to pay attention. Deflecting attacks at the right moment is fundamental, and you'll still need to adjust your approach to combat to shift between offensive and defensive tactics depending on what's unfolding. But once I understood what the game wanted from me, its combat stopped feeling like a wall I couldn't break through.

Fighting enemies is fast and flashy, and Wo Long 2 introduces the Focus system, which adds more combat mechanics to broaden the possibilities, and makes you depend less on deflecting incoming attacks. First, you'll need to build up Spirit, which is essentially a combat momentum meter returning from the first game. You build Spirit by hitting enemies and deflecting attacks. Deflecting is particularly effective as it drains the enemy's Spirit too. However, taking hits will push your Spirit in the negative direction. If the negative side fills up, you'll suffer Spirit Disruption, leaving you stunned and vulnerable.

The Spirit Focus Deflect move uses Spirit to counter circular red attacks. It's stronger than the normal deflect, and sends enemies flying backwards, potentially knocking foes into each other. It can also bounce some ranged attacks back at enemies. Focus Jump uses Spirit to deal with linear red attacks, so instead of just parrying, you'll jump over or through the attack to kick airborne enemies down to the ground. Without using this, enemies can pummel you from above, so it's an important mechanic to master.

I'm not going to pretend I suddenly became a souls-like expert, but I wasn't frustrated by Wo Long 2 in the way I expected to be. For someone who doesn't naturally gravitate to souls-likes, playing them can sometimes feel overwhelming. Wo Long 2 is more interested in showing me how it works before becoming too punishing. The result is that I began to notice things I probably wouldn't have appreciated if I spent the entire preview session panicking about dying. The open-world structure meant I could explore more, the combat was more approachable without being too easy, and the various systems made sense from the start. 

Don't get me wrong: I'm probably still going to swear at it, there will almost certainly be bosses that make me wonder why I'm even playing it, and I'll definitely still make catastrophic tactical mistakes, but I still want to play more. Wo Long 2 has convinced me that I don't actually hate souls-likes, but I'm probably still not going to go and finish the Elden Ring DLC.

event_model_payload.headline: James Pond Legacy Situation Is More Than Meets The AI
event_model_payload.summary:
Last month, System 3 Software released a trailer for James Pond Legacy, a four-game collection for Nintendo Switch 2. But the gameplay footage was largely overshadowed by accusations its developer used generative AI to create the game's promotional artwork and cover. System 3 followed this trailer up with a blog post asserting that generative AI was not used in the development process for James Pond Legacy, but some wires were evidently crossed. 

If you go back and watch that trailer, it's not difficult to see why viewers pointed out the AI-like quality of the 3D characters adorning the game's box art and other promotional material. When System 3 responded to the accusations with the assertion that "no generative AI was used in the creation of the artwork," referring specifically to the Bovine Bomber character, this was based on the information it was given at the time by Antstream, the studio that handled the collection's actual development. 

"That was the statement that we were given at the time by Antstream," System 3 CEO Mark Cale told GameSpot during a call. "We weren't involved in the process. They supplied all of the artwork and they supplied, in the process, the [work-in-progress] illustration. All of that was given to us." 

Cale later provided GameSpot with the statement it received back in December from Antstream, well before the trailer was made public. 


"The art pipeline on some non-in-game assets includes algorithm-assisted depth and form translation: Original 2D concepts are input into a model to estimate volume and lighting, producing pseudo-3D drafts," reads the statement from Antstream. "Artists then manually repaint, re-render, and finalise all illustrations using this pipeline. The final assets are fully human-authored, with algorithms used only for intermediate visualisation." 

You may notice that the statement omits the term "AI," which led to some internal confusion. 

"We requested this [statement] for use across the board, including Steam, and to address applicable requirements under the EU Artificial Intelligence Act, including the transparency provisions that took effect on August 2, 2026," Cale explained. "Antstream now argues that, because we requested the statement for these purposes, we must have known the extent of their use of AI. However, their statement expressly describes the final assets as 'fully human-authored,' with algorithms used 'only for intermediate visualisation.'" 

Had the use of generative AI been made clearer prior to the publication of the trailer and the blog post, System 3 would have taken a different approach, Cale said. 

"That doesn't say 'generative AI,'" Cale said. "And if they've used any generative AI at all, it should have been clear in that statement. That was the statement we were told to put on to Nintendo, to Steam, PS5, Xbox--any format we want to go based on that. The actual gameplay itself is, of course, all emulated anyway. And for me, I don't know the definition of how you're going to try to say something that's prompt-based [is] 'generative AI' versus algorithms. And so we honestly looked at that and took that honestly to [mean] there was no AI." 

GameSpot was unable to reach Antstream for comment during our time investigating the situation.

Cale said he is far from wanting to throw Antstream under the bus for what happened. He explained the reason Antstream was contracted for the project was because it had done "a bloody good job" of emulating games for past compilations, such as The Last Ninja Collection. The situation for James Pond was a little different, though, with little in the way of existing concept art or other production designs to go on for the in-game supplemental materials. 

As someone wary, to put it mildly, of any generative AI usage in video games, I told Cale I would have preferred hand-drawn material created specifically for the collection based on past artwork, but Cale said it wasn't feasible. 

"All of the artwork that has been created within the Pond-verse has been based on art that's either on the box cover or characters that are in the game," he said. "And at the end of the day, if people think we're going to redraw, re-render to that quality, and have 20 or 30 people working two years on it, forget it: It's not going to happen. We wouldn't put the Pond-verse in there. The simple fact is, it would not match an investment versus a return. I'm only speaking for myself--I can't speak for Antstream--but if it was for me, I wouldn't do it, because I couldn't justify having 20 artists for a year create all of that in that way." 

Still, Cale said that full disclosure--and a clearer set of guidelines for what System 3 considers generative AI--should help to avoid another situation like this happening in the future. Having a set, and perhaps broader, definition for what constitutes generative AI will, at the very least, help prospective buyers know what they're purchasing. 

It won't completely solve the problem, though, as Cale mentioned the need to be careful about using the term "AI" to describe any element in a game--even some that have existed for decades. 

"AI's become such a swear word, and you should quote me on that!" Cale said. "So, you know, we're doing this other game. It's all been hand-done and everything, and I can't even say, 'Opponent AI's been tweaked to do this.' No, it's 'opponent behavior.' It's just madness! I just don't want to use the word 'AI' in anything, as far as I'm concerned, anymore." 

James Pond Legacy: The Pond is Not Enough doesn't have a final release date yet, but will launch exclusively on Nintendo Switch 2 at the end of October.

event_model_payload.headline: GTA 6 Soundtrack – All Confirmed Songs So Far
event_model_payload.summary:
Following the GTA 6 Extended Look, songs from the GTA 6 soundtrack have started to be compiled into playlists thanks to the mammoth 25-minute trailer's heap of new confirmed tracks. There are a host of great tracks that I can't stop humming, so what better way to enjoy them than a curated playlist that you can stick on repeat to learn every word ahead of the game's release?

There are electronica-laden retro hits that suit the Vice City vibes of Leonida through to modern rock tracks that'll have you singing their catchy hooks as you cruise the streets. Below is the full list of GTA 6 soundtrack titles from the Extended Look and all of the trailers so far.

Full GTA 6 soundtrack so far

Here are all of the songs in the GTA 6 soundtrack so far, as well as where they first appeared in GTA 6 marketing:

  • Tom Petty - Love is a Long Road (Trailer 1)
  • The Pointer Sisters - Hot Together (Trailer 2)
  • Wang Cheung - Everybody Have Fun Tonight (Trailer 2)
  • Zenglen - Child Support (Trailer 2)

  • Birdman ft. Lil Wayne - Pop Bottles (Extended Look, 0:08)
  • Sexyy Red and Tay Keith - Pound Town (Extended Look, 0:50)

  • Aluna and Jayda G - Mine O' Mine (Extended Look, 22:03)
  • Bob Moses and Elderbrook - Inner Light (Extended Look, 25:44)

GTA 6 rumored or teased songs

Of course, alongside the official GTA 6 soundtrack so far, there have been rumors, teasers, and leaked songs.

Travis Scott

In September 2026, Travis Scott posted a GTA 6-style teaser of some extremely high heels and tagged Rockstar Games in the caption on his Instagram profile, all but confirming that the rapper will have music featured in the game.

However, back in July 2025 he also teased his appearance in the game. Scott released the music video for his track 2000 Excursion featuring a car with the license plate "GTA6 VI6."

Morgan Wallen

On the same day that Travis Scott teased his involvement with GTA 6, American country-pop artist Morgan Wallen posted an image on X of some poolside steps that are unmistakably in the GTA 6 art style.

Panama and Poolside - Back to Life

Panama said that Back to Life, made with Poolside, would appear in GTA 6 in a now-deleted Instagram comment. The track subsequently appeared in the GTA 6 leaks.

Skrilla - Doot Doot (6 7)

Skrilla publicly said that Doot Doot would be in GTA 6, and noted that he would be able to play his own music in the game. Of course, another one of his tracks went on to feature in the Extended Look trailer in the form of Kodak Black.

Neon Indian - Polish Girl

Neon Indian teased that his relationship with Rockstar isn't finished following his music's GTA 5 appearance during a podcast appearance.

Freddie Gibbs

Freddie Gibbs is rumored to be involved in GTA 6 thanks to an interview that content creator HipHopGamer did with PC Gamer. He claimed, "There are things in Grand Theft Auto that I know for a fact, because I got a chance to party with Rockstar." He went on to say that "a major rapper that left CM Punk bloody by accident," features in one of the game's side missions. Freddie Gibbs revealed that he accidentally hurt the wrestler while filming the 2025 horror Night Patrol.

The track in question was featured in GTA 5 on the Radio Los Santos station, so we can't be sure it's this track making a return.

ScHoolboy Q

ScHoolboy Q seemingly confirmed his return to the franchise in a Twitter reply, too. Celebrating the 10-year anniversary of his major label debut Oxymoron in February 2024, one now-suspended fan account replied, "As long as you drop some heat for Grand Theft Auto 6 radio, we all Gucci." The musician confirmed, "Ima be on there, don't even trip."

T-Pain

In early January 2024, T-Pain confirmed that he is working with Rockstar Games on GTA 6. During a livestream, he explained that he used to be an active member of the GTA role-playing server NoPixel before being asked to quit because of the conflict of interest.

Apparently, Rockstar told him that he "couldn't do role-play anymore because it kind of goes against [their rules]." T-Pain explained that Rockstar likened it to someone re-recording one of his albums and listening to it instead of the original. "Then I started working on the game with them," he finished.

Megan Thee Stallion

Back in March 2025, Megan Thee Stallion shared a behind-the-scenes video from a photo shoot on her Instagram stories. In the clip Megan is wearing a bikini and posing with a bottle in front of a familiar palm tree backdrop.

A similar background was used in the GTA 6 promotional artwork, and fans believe that Megan could be working with Rockstar in a starring role. However, later on Megan Thee Stallion posted the same video as part of an advert for her Chicas Divertidas tequila.

Ski Mask the Slump God

The artist posted on Instagram confirming that both he and the late XXXTentacion have tracks in GTA 6, but stopped short of confirming which songs would feature.

event_model_payload.headline: Dredge Has Never Been Cheaper, So Grab This Lovecraftian Fishing Adventure At An All-Time Low
event_model_payload.summary:
Sometimes, I simply enjoy reeling people into playing a delightful indie, and Dredge… well, Dredge is one of those times. It’s a fishing game, yes, but it’s one that hides a Lovecraftian selection of horrors beneath the surface of what, at first, seems fairly tame. If you’re not quite ready for the sheer panic of the best horror games but still want something with spooky vibes, Dredge is what you’re looking for, and right now, it’s cheaper than ever.

As someone who doesn’t like the idea of fishing, it surprised me that Dredge ended up becoming one of my favorite indie games. That’s helped by the fact that it’s not really about fishing, at least not in the traditional sense. Instead, it’s about making your boat better with your spoils and eventually finding the courage to head out at night. And trust me, you’ll want to brave it.

At the beginning, going out in the dark is a good way to lose. As you experience the story of this interesting world, you’ll inevitably find ways to make trips that were once too dangerous, while also gaining the ability to travel farther and visit different towns. Even during the day, there are still risks, but nothing compares to the horrors you’ll encounter once the sun goes down.

The more you let your panic rise, the more likely you are to see deadly creatures, like a phantom shark or a giant crab disguised as a shipwreck. There have been plenty of times when I’ve driven my little ship as fast as possible to avoid enemies, and in reality, the tension and panic rushing through my body have been surprisingly high, considering I’m used to playing horror games and watching scary movies.

Dredge is one of those indies that, if you’re even somewhat intrigued by the premise, you need to give it a try. There are very few indies—or games in general—that manage to blend something I’d find truly boring with a world that is genuinely interesting, then somehow make the two fit together. Dredge is a truly solid experience, and while the opening is a little slow, it’s well worth getting into… especially if you can find it on deal.

Fortunately, that time has come. Right now, you can get a Steam key for Dredge for just $8.87 / £7.80 at Fanatical. That’s 65% off the listed price and lower than Steam has ever had the game, so you’re getting it at a great time. Just make sure you dim the lights—or turn them off completely—put those headphones on, and get immersed.

It’s almost a cozy experience, if not for the eldritch horrors.

event_model_payload.summary:
A fresh batch of games are coming to the PlayStation Plus Game Catalog for Extra- and Premium-tier subscribers, but several games are also on their way out. While we don't have an exact date for their exit just yet, there'll be seven games in total leaving soon, so you only have a few weeks left to play one of the best survival-horrors of all time and a melodramatic gangland adventure where you can hit people really hard on the head with a baseball bat.

PlayStation Plus Game Catalog games leaving soon

  • Silent Hill 2
  • Yakuza: Like a Dragon
  • Gloomhaven: Mercenaries Edition
  • Jurassic World Evolution 2
  • Rogue Lords
  • Lake
  • Death Squared

The biggest departure on the list is easily the Silent Hill 2 remake from Bloober Team, and it's leaving right before the start of spooky season. While the original Silent Hill 2 was long considered to be one of the greatest psychological-horror games of all time, the remake improved on it tremendously, offering more than just updated visuals and modernized gameplay. Dynamic combat is balanced by smarter enemy AI, while the titular Silent Hill is expanded with new locations and puzzles to create an explorable world full of suspense.

Critically acclaimed upon its 2024 release, it's one of several new entries that have helped kickstart a Silent Hill renaissance. The next chapter in the series, Silent Hill Townfall, launches on September 24, and this spin-off will see players explore a spooky Scottish town, using their handheld TV to stay a step ahead of the creatures haunting the local streets. Bloober Team is also working on a remake of the first Silent Hill game.

Yakuza: Like a Dragon was a major departure from its predecessors. Not only did it feature a brand-new protagonist in the form of Ichiban Kasuga, but the gameplay also went from beat-'em-up brawling to turn-based RPG action. First arriving in late 2020, it's another great Yakuza game that combines a surprisingly heartfelt story with goofy moments and a likable cast of rogues. While the turn-based gameplay can be a grind--especially in the endgame--it's still worth checking out. Fans of the Yakuza franchise have eaten well since then, as we've gotten a sequel to Ichiban's first adventure, Like a Dragon: Infinite Wealth, as well as several spin-off games and remakes.

Don't forget, all PlayStation Plus subscribers can grab four freebies right now--Sniper Elite: Resistance, MLB The Show 26, Chained Echoes, and Wobbly Life. The PlayStation Plus Game Catalog is also adding Runescape: Dragonwilds and WWE 2K26 today, and it'll be updated with more games like Ball X Pit, Slitterhead, and Ninja Gaiden: Ragebound over the next couple of weeks.

event_model_payload.summary:
Each time you start a new campaign in Afterworld, Paradox's upcoming post-apocalyptic grand strategy game, a tiny virtual historian cracks their knuckles and gets to work writing a new 200-year history for what happened to North America in the dying days of the great war.

They will decide where the great powers fired their nuclear-tipped missiles, where they released their clouds of flesh-eating nanites, where they dropped their lung-bubbling chemical weapons, and they will decide who survived and who died. These procedural changes should mean that each time you start a new game of Afterworld, the map will be dramatically different from the last.

That flexibility to rewrite the surface of Afterworld is vital, game director Dan Lind tells me, "Otherwise it undermines a lot of the exploration".

Valve have sometimes – if perhaps not often enough to call it a grand old tradition – massaged interest in their hardware by pairing the kit with a new game. For the Steam Deck it was Aperture Desk Job, and for 2019’s jammy sod of a VR headset, the Valve Index, it was Half-Life: Alyx, a full-length City 17 adventure that reviewer Graham (RPS in peace) called “a masterclass of first-person shooter design.”

Still, people rarely want to take the same class twice, hence why padding-compacted eyebrows have been raised by Alyx again being a tentpole of the new Steam Frame headset – this time, to showcase the game running in PC-less, standalone VR. Why not make something new, even a smaller tech demo like ADJ or the Index’s own The Lab collection of Portal-themed minigames?

According to Valve staff, several of whom I spoke to prior to the Frame’s Monday night launch, there were several reasons why a return to Alyx was considered more valuable – even though a brand new VR game was, at least briefly, on the table.

event_model_payload.headline: Rockstar had a mole in the union worker Discord server "for over two and a half years", GTA 6 company reveals during legal battle
event_model_payload.summary:
Back in October 2025, GTA 6 developers Rockstar fired a group of 34, mostly UK-based employees on a charge of "gross misconduct", alleging that they had risked the leaking of confidential information while posting on a Discord server set up by union organisers. The ousted UK workers and their representatives have since taken Rockstar to court, accusing the company of getting rid of them to stop their union gaining enough members to win official recognition under UK law.

This week, both parties filed opening submissions at an employment tribunal in Glasgow, which Rockstar parent company Take-Two Interactive have emailed to RPS and Game Developer, among others. Taken together, the filings amount to over 100 pages of claims and counterclaims, with thousands of pages of evidence to be discussed in the coming weeks. Amongst other things, the docs give us more sense of events leading up to the dismissals, including the revelation that Rockstar had a mole or "whistleblower" passing them information on the people using the Discord server.
